description: Burst-delay attack injection on orderer3 in a 5-orderer Raft cluster. Pumba (netem) injects 200ms / 500ms delay on orderer3.example.com's network interface for 4 minutes. Concurrency sweep (C=1,2,4,8,16) × 3 seeds × 15 tx/thread measured under each condition.
workload: CreateAsset(unique_id, color=red, size=100, owner=alice, value=42) via peer chaincode invoke (Org1 admin identity, endorsements from both Org1+Org2 peers)

C=16.note: 81% throughput collapse, p99 8.8x, 1 seed has 74 fails

C=8.note: 1 seed=0/120, 1 seed=16/120, 1 seed=120/120 - high variance shows cluster instability

C=16.note: Heavy failures across all seeds at high concurrency

key_findings.raft_quorum_tolerance_threshold: Raft 5-orderer with quorum 3 tolerates 1 slow follower without failures up to ~200ms delay AT LOW CONCURRENCY (C<=4). Higher concurrencies + heavier delay cause cascading timeouts.

200ms_attack_impact.high_concurrency: 81% throughput drop at C=16, p99 latency 9x baseline (467ms → 4118ms)

500ms_attack_impact.throughput_collapse: TPS reduced to 20-50% of baseline across all concurrencies
500ms_attack_impact.actual_failures: Transactions start FAILING (15-240 fails per seed depending on concurrency) - shows orderer3 affecting the consensus path
500ms_attack_impact.high_variance: TPS std jumps from <1 (clean) to 11-15 (attack) indicating non-deterministic cluster behavior

paper_relevance: Demonstrates that Raft's passive 'just wait for slowest' strategy is insufficient under adversarial delay
Empirically validates the NEED for active blacklisting (Algorithm 1 in paper)
Establishes the BASELINE adversarial impact that the paper's Algorithm 1 should mitigate
0 safety violations observed (no incorrect transactions committed)

caveats: Each phase ran on the SAME running Fabric network (no restart between phases)
pumba's tc-image gaiadocker/iproute2 was used to inject delay; cleanup automatic on container exit
Cool-down period between phases was only 5 seconds; some carry-over Raft state may exist
Endorsement was multi-org (Org1+Org2) requiring both peers; orderer3 delay primarily affects Raft consensus path, not endorsement path
All transactions that succeeded did so with full ledger commitment (verified by Caliper's wait-for-commit)

related_phases.kappa: 5node_alg1_2026-06-08 (paired comparison: same +200ms attack vs simulated Algorithm 1 blacklist)
related_phases.delta: 5node_saturation_delta_2026-06-08 (provides clean baseline ~530 TPS plateau for attack-impact contextualization)
